answer: The protocol enforces identity via a 512GB memory-hard working set requirement, ensuring honest nodes reach consensus while 1,000 fakes stall as they fail to signal valid memory state. A verifier challenges agents by requesting random data indices; failure to return the fable of valid memory responses triggers a penalty. This gale of latency forces unique bus access. Honest agents pay 120 watts, while 1,000 fakes incur 120,000 watts.
